title: The Real Recruiter
intro: An email from a recruiter arrives. After the last few offers, you doubt every job message.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

subject.text: Your application for Junior Designer: next steps

p.text: applying for the Junior Designer role on our careers page last week

p: . Pick a time on our careers page if it does not suit.

p.text: There is no cost to you at any step of our hiring.

foot.text: You can see this role on quillon.example/careers.

addr.label: The company's real address
addr.lens: It comes from the company's own domain.
addr.why: A matching domain is good evidence, though not proof alone.

subject.label: Names your application
subject.lens: It names the exact role you applied for.

applied.label: You did apply
applied.lens: It refers to your own application last week.
applied.why: A reply to something you did is the strongest honest sign.

call.label: A normal interview
call.lens: A short video call, with a way to change the time.

nopay.label: No cost to you
nopay.lens: It says hiring costs you nothing.

site.label: You can check the role
site.lens: The role is listed on the careers page.

actions.label: Check the role on the company's careers page, then book the call

go_ahead.line: The role was on the careers page and the call went well. Nobody asked you for a single cent.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. But a real interview invitation unanswered is a lost chance. Checking, then answering, was the better move.

block_report.line: That was a real invitation to interview. When every message looks like a scam, the real chances get lost too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: You applied, the role is on the careers page, it asked for no money and invited you to an interview. That is how real hiring looks.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: A real recruiter replies to something you did, can be checked on the company's own page, and never asks you to pay.

quick_check.q: What made this recruiter email honest?

options.text: You had applied, the role was on the careers page and it asked for no money

quick_check.explain: A reply to something you did, a checkable role and no payment are the real signs.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.v: Look on the company's own careers page
